I5.quote: Chromium-based metal-organic framework (MOF), MIL-101(Cr), has emerged as a potential hydrogen storage material because of its high specific surface area, tuneable pore size, and unique structure.

notes: The carbon sorbent is the commercial activated carbon measured on its own ('The AC (WS-480) was obtained from Chemviron carbon.', main p. 2, Section 2.1): 3.7 wt% (414.4 cc/g) at 77 K, its isotherm plotted in Figure 6 (main p. 6) to about 6000 kPa, BET 946.96 m2/g. The AC@MIL-101 composites contain only 0.63-2.5 wt% carbon (main p. 3, Section 2.4), so they are MOF-majority and not carbon sorbents; MIL-101 and the SI's HKUST-1 samples are MOFs. The H2 method is not named as volumetric in the text; the instrument is a BELSORP-HP automated high-pressure gas adsorption system, a volumetric (Sieverts-type) apparatus, and He is listed among the gases 'used for the adsorption studies'. Table I gives 'up to 6000 kPa', so each tabulated uptake is taken at the isotherm's highest pressure, which Figure 6's pressure axis recovers. No retraction statement; record is_retracted false. The paper says only that its MIL-101 value 'is in good agreement with the reported data [36]', not that its values were published before, so duplicate_data does not apply.
